title: Outbox completion requires durable handoff; reclaim is attempt-bounded
decision:
`MessagePublisher` success means durable broker/store acceptance that survives an
offline consumer. Core ships no lossy PubSub adapter as the outbox default; an absent or
non-durable publisher is a visible configuration failure and never marks a row published.
Expired `publishing` rows with `attempts >= maxAttempts` transition directly to `dead`.
Only the remainder returns to `pending`. Envelope reconstruction is inside the fenced
failure path, so repeated corruption also exhausts attempts and becomes terminal.
rationale:
Inbox deduplication can absorb duplicates after a durable handoff, but cannot recover a
message discarded before any durable consumer queue existed. Attempt accounting must
advance on claim and terminate independently of whether the dying worker ran cleanup.

sections.title: Consequences
sections.text:
P5.12 proves offline publish/restart delivery, crash-expiry-reclaim exhaustion and corrupt
envelope exhaustion. P14 may consume the envelope but may not reinterpret lossy PubSub as
durable acknowledgement.
